item.title: The last war isn't the next one; Asia and US defense fundamentals remain strong
item.dc:creator: Bank of America
item.description: Bank of America · Global Research Unlocked — Defense restocking accelerates; new threats drive demand Defense demand remains strong globally as depleted inventories, shifting threats and years of underinvestment drive a multiyear restocking cycle. Ron Epstein discusses record US defense outlays, rising production needs and why recent weakness in defense stocks may be disconnected from the fundamentals. KJ Hwang highlights Korea's expansion beyond the land systems that drove early exports. Korean companies are expending into air defense, low-cost interceptors and counter-drone technologies, with the Gulf emerging as a potential source of new orders. Together they also discuss how militaries are balancing inexpensive drones with sophisticated missile threats, and why lessons from today's conflicts may not necessarily translate to how the next wars may be fought. item.title: AI Boom Faces a Higher-Yield Roadblock
item.dc:creator: Morgan Stanley
item.description: Morgan Stanley · Thoughts on the Market — Our ABS Strategist Carolyn Campbell explains how rising borrowing costs are slowing the AI data center boom and what could drive a rebound in financing. Read more insights from Morgan Stanley. ----- Transcript ----- Carolyn Campbell: Welcome to Thoughts on the Market. I'm Carolyn Campbell, Morgan Stanley's Asset-Backed Securities Strategist. Today, why the AI boom is running into an unexpected obstacle: the cost of borrowing money. It's Friday, October 16th, at 10am in New York. Demand for data center facilities is booming. Yet even as companies race to build more capacity, the financing for them is becoming increasingly expensive. And that tension is creating an interesting story in credit markets. Since January, five-year Treasury rates have climbed more than one percentage point, and spreads for data center assets have also gone wider. At the beginning of 2026, the highest-rated data center bonds offered yields below 5 percent. Today, similar bonds are yielding closer to 7 percent, and that increase matters enormously for companies trying to finance multi-billion-dollar facilities. item.description: RBC Capital Markets · Macro Minutes — A broad tour of global FX markets spanning Asia, G10, and LatAm, covering key currency trades, positioning, and central bank divergence. The discussion highlights major risks into year-end, including an AI-trade pullback, China trade tensions, US Treasury moves, and political uncertainty in Brazil. Participants: Elsa Lignos (Desk Strategy), Global Head of FX Strategy & Head of EMEA Institutional FX Sales Abbas Keshvani (Desk Strategy), Asia Macro Strategist Luis Estrada (Desk Strategy), LATAM FX Strategist * Research Analyst opinions are their published views, independent of those expressed by Desk Analysts
